The draft is safe. It drops the quality session, so there is no pace work on a sore Achilles. Every run is flat and easy, with heart-rate and pace caps. It tells Johnny to get the Achilles looked at and gives daily stop rules that depend on whether it feels the same or better each day. Volume falls slightly, from 31 to about 29 mi (5+6+4+4+10). The long run drops to 10 mi with no marathon-pace finish. Both questions get direct, honest answers: keep running easy, but only under these conditions, and seriousness is a call for a physio or doctor, not the coach. The fixed Monday and Friday rest days are kept, and the cautious approach fits his shin-splint history. Each day can be run as written, with swap-outs if the Achilles gets worse.

I took it down from a 5 for two reasons. Monday and Friday are called "travel days", which the card doesn't support. The visible plan also never mentions the 15 November race date or taper timing, and his anxiety about the block gets little direct reassurance. A stricter coach might also want two or three days completely off, since the Achilles is tender to press and got sharper under load.
